clue.text: Strongly criticise a course of action taken by team's leader

the leader of the team is the word's opening letter

parts.note: a tack is a course of action or approach, as in 'try a different tack'

explanation.surface: A captain is blamed for a tactical decision the team was led into.
explanation.definitionFit: To attack an idea or person can mean to criticise them harshly, a figurative sense of assault.

clue.text: One who judges fools accordingly, right?

parts.note: asses are fools
so means therefore or accordingly

explanation.surface: Someone sitting in judgement is asked whether they treat idiots as such.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor evaluates or adjudicates, for example valuing property or advising a court.

clue.text: Boy following sailor wearing waterproof stuff

indicators.note: the boy comes after the sailor

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
Paul is a boy's name
in means wearing, as in 'in a hat'

explanation.surface: A lad trails behind a seaman who has his oilskins on.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarpaulin is heavy waterproof canvas used for covers, so it is waterproof material.

clue.text: Floor show act dancing round naked

the letters of act are set dancing into a new order

parts.note: bare means naked

explanation.surface: A nightclub turn features a performer dancing in the nude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'act' looks like the performance being described, but it is anagram fodder, with 'dancing' scrambling it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is entertainment performed in a nightclub or restaurant while the audience sits at tables, traditionally called a floor show.

clue.text: Rogue's unlimited guarantee — be taken in

indicators.note: be is taken in, placed inside the trimmed guarantee
without its limits, the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a warranty is a guarantee

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' reads as a noun, but here it is the adjective meaning straying from the norm.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, rogue means deviating from the norm, as in a rogue result, which is the meaning of aberrant.

clue.text: Similarly, purchase an identical disc on the phone

indicators.note: words heard over the phone are judged by their sound, so the word for purchase is taken as it sounds

parts.note: to purchase is to buy
an identical one is the same one
a token can be a disc used in place of a coin

explanation.surface: Someone rings up to order a matching coin or counter.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means for the same reason or in the same way, so it is a synonym for similarly.

clue.text: Do Parma when travelling? It's a plan for the future

indicators.note: travelling letters move about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A tourist needs a guide to find Parma while touring Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a road map is a strategy setting out steps toward a goal, like a route on a chart.

clue.text: Protection regularly taken by American soldiers

regularly means taking every other letter of the word taken

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: US troops routinely provide cover.

clue.text: Difficult problem? Student's lost heart

parts.note: a stickler can be a knotty problem or puzzle

explanation.definitionFit: Ticker is informal slang for the heart, which ticks like a clock.

clue.text: Pipe to be attached to both taps? Can't decide

parts.note: to pipe is to blow, as through a pipe or whistle

parts.words: to be attached to both taps
parts.note: a sink's two taps are the hot and the cold, so a pipe joined to both is joined to these

explanation.definitionFit: To blow hot and cold is an idiom for vacillating, keep changing one's mind.

clue.text: Clean axe

definitions.meaning: to clean by rubbing hard with a brush
to axe is to cancel or call off a plan

explanation.surface: Wash a hatchet.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to scour clean and, informally, to cancel something, as with axe.

clue.text: Sluggish? Teach girl exercises

indicators.note: the letters are exercised, put through movements into a new order

explanation.surface: A sleepy child needs a coach to get her moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic means lacking energy and slow, the same as sluggish.

clue.text: Bird's extremely sharp weapon

indicators.note: extremely means the extremes, the first and last letters of the word sharp

parts.note: an arrow is a weapon

explanation.surface: A bird's beak is a pointed weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a familiar small brown songbird.

clue.text: As one new service in heart of Greece

indicators.note: the new service sits inside those central letters
the heart of the word Greece is its central pair of letters

parts.note: Mass is a church service

clue.text: What may be said of chess film?

definitions.text: What may be said of chess film?

parts.words: What may be said of chess film?
parts.note: chess is a game for exactly two players, and the phrase is also the title of a 1962 British comedy film starring Peter Sellers

explanation.surface: A reviewer sums up a movie about chess.
explanation.walkthrough: The title belongs to a 1962 Peter Sellers comedy, and the phrase is also simply true of chess.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-player game permits a single pair of players, and the same words name a classic British film.

clue.text: Reptile having a breather after climbing a rocky peak

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a gill is what a fish breathes with
a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A lizard pauses for breath after scaling a crag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns GILL into LLIG. A tor is a rocky hill, common in the English West Country.
explanation.definitionFit: The alligator is a large reptile of the crocodile family.

clue.text: Exploit unusually large survey of voters

indicators.note: unusually means the letters are arranged in an unusual way

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone takes advantage of an unexpectedly big opinion poll.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit poll questions people as they leave polling stations to forecast an election result.

clue.text: Fat: felt anxious, terribly uncertain as to what should be done

definitions.text: uncertain as to what should be done

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters are put in a very bad, so jumbled, order

explanation.surface: A dieter, worried about weight, is unsure what to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat' looks like part of the definition, but its letters go into the anagram with 'felt anxious'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a situation in constant change, so it fits being undecided about the right course.

clue.text: Cato, say, first to recognise advantage being in group

indicators.note: the letters are put inside the group

parts.note: a set is a group

indicators.note: first to means the opening letter of the word recognise

parts.note: van is short for advantage in tennis scoring

explanation.definitionFit: Clouseau's houseboy and sparring partner is an example of a domestic employee.

clue.text: Joyful number hugging remainder heading off

indicators.note: the number wraps around the trimmed remainder

parts.note: five is a number

parts.note: the rest is the remainder

explanation.definitionFit: Festive means celebratory and merry, suiting a joyful occasion.

clue.text: Roman poet's verse, one girl translated

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: translated means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl translates a line of Latin poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges I and GIRL into IRGIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil was the Roman poet who wrote the Aeneid.

clue.text: Certainly relieved, ultimately, after home covered

indicators.note: the other pieces come after the home piece

parts.note: in means at home
sure means certainly, as in 'sure, I will'

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of relieved

explanation.surface: Someone is relieved to learn they are protected now they are back home.
explanation.definitionFit: Being insured means having a policy that covers you against loss.

clue.text: Sketch includes river border

indicators.note: the sketch takes the river letter inside it

parts.note: a skit is a comic sketch

explanation.surface: A comedy scene is set beside a riverbank.

clue.text: Once viewed old things in another way

indicators.note: the letters are put in another way, a different order

explanation.surface: Antiques are looked at afresh.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means as soon as something is seen, so immediately once viewed.

clue.text: Aim to include Italian individual in act, without the help of others

definitions.text: act, without the help of others

indicators.note: the aim takes the Italian inside it

one is a single individual

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to proceed independently, so to act unaided by others.

clue.text: Keen on catching start of record, the first few bars

indicators.note: the keen-on word catches the letter inside it

parts.note: into means keen on, as in 'into jazz'

indicators.note: the start of the word record is its opening letter

explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the introductory passage of a song, the opening bars before the main part.

clue.text: Lead's initial approach, first time away in play

indicators.note: the initial of the word lead is its opening letter
first says it is the earlier of the two time letters in the approach that goes
away means taken out of the approach

parts.note: an attitude is an approach or way of thinking

explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a theatre piece but is the definition: freedom to move. 'away' removes the first T of ATTITUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Play can mean freedom of movement or scope, as in a rope with some play, which is latitude.

clue.text: Fuel supplied by dear character endlessly

parts.note: pet is a term of endearment like dear

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a role is a character played by an actor

explanation.surface: A loved one in a play provides the energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrol is the British term for gasoline, the fuel for cars.
